subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool treats subprocess nonzero exit codes as tool failures, masking stdout and exit-code semantics

question: Should completed exec results with nonzero exit codes be nonfatal agent results by default across embedded-agent and isolated cron surfaces?
rationale: Current code has competing semantics: the exec runtime treats normal nonzero exits as completed, but shared result classification and cron state still treat the same result as a tool failure.

options.title: Make normal nonzero exits nonfatal
options.body: Update the shared classifier and cron/embedded-agent tests so completed exec exit codes preserve stdout/stderr and diagnostics without setting tool failure state.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in semantics
options.body: Keep the current default but add a documented accepted-exit or nonfatal-exit policy surface, accepting extra configuration and upgrade complexity.

options.title: Keep failure semantics
options.body: Document wrapper-based workarounds and close the behavior as intentional, accepting that semantic-exit cron jobs must force exit 0.

recommendation.title: Make normal nonzero exits nonfatal
recommendation.body: Update the shared classifier and cron/embedded-agent tests so completed exec exit codes preserve stdout/stderr and diagnostics without setting tool failure state.

likelyOwner.reason: The history ties this owner to both the exec outcome helper refactor and the merged lower-layer nonzero-exit behavior.
